# Review checklist

Read this when reviewing an existing workflow/state-graph design or checking a single claim in one.
A review is a findings list against the required artifact, not a rewrite. Where the design is
silent, the finding is "not stated", which is a defect for load-bearing rows and a note otherwise.

## Contents

- Rejection findings
- Completeness findings
- Review output

## Rejection findings

Any of these is a request-changes finding on its own:

| Finding | What to look for | Required correction |
|---|---|---|
| Checkpoint-equals-exactly-once | Any sentence in which a checkpoint, cache, or successful model turn is offered as proof an effect ran once | Effect row with replay-safety class, receipt, and reconciliation |
| Automatic replay of an unknown effect | Retry, resume, or replay path that re-dispatches while an effect is `UNKNOWN` | Persist `UNKNOWN`; reconcile before any retry |
| Reused key with mismatched intent accepted | Key derived from node or run alone; no intent digest comparison before dispatch | Intent-bound key; reject mismatch before dispatch |
| Retention shorter than the retry or ambiguity window | Tombstone TTL below the longest retry schedule plus reconciliation delay | Retention ≥ retry window + ambiguity window + late-arrival slack |
| Approval not bound to exact action and state | Approval carries no target, candidate identity, expiry, or resumed-state check | Bind all five; re-check on resume |
| Admission without capacity, fairness, backpressure, or liveness | A queue with no bound, no tenant rule, no shed policy, or no heartbeat/lease | Complete the scheduling contract |
| Cancellation without semantics | "Cancellable" with no cooperative/durable split or in-flight and late-worker disposition | State both semantics and both dispositions |
| Checkpoint resume presented as deterministic replay | Snapshot store described with replay vocabulary, or handlers assumed not to repeat | Name one recovery model and what repeats |
| Unbounded cycle | A back edge with no iteration, time, token, or cost bound | Add the bound and show the reachable exit |
| Missing terminal states | Graph "ends" implicitly; no terminal node per outcome class | Named terminals with required evidence |
| Taint dropped at a handoff | A packet or edge payload that omits evidence and taint labels present upstream | Carry labels unchanged across every edge |
| Model-selected edge without an allowed set | A router that "picks the next step" with no destination set or deterministic guardrail | Enumerate destinations; add guardrails |
| Isolation claimed from delegation | A separate worker or context window offered as an authority boundary | State the real control: credential scope, tool absence, or a policy boundary |
| Runtime chosen inside the design | The artifact selects a framework as a consequence of being graph-shaped | Move to section 14 as deferred criteria; note the owner decision needed |

## Completeness findings

For each of the fourteen artifact sections, check that it is present, in order, and either filled
or marked not applicable with a reason. Then check:

- every supplied identity (prompt, tool, schema, grader, model, runtime revision) appears in
  section 2 — a supplied identity that is omitted is a finding;
- every effect node in section 4 has a row in section 9;
- every fan-out edge in section 5 has a policy in section 7;
- every failure class in section 8 has exactly one retry owner;
- every cycle in section 5 has a bound in section 11;
- every claim is labelled `[verified]`, `[sourced]`, or `[unverified]`, and no static claim is
  presented as runtime proof.

## Review output

1. Verdict: `accept`, `accept with findings`, or `request changes` — request changes whenever a
   rejection finding stands.
2. Findings ranked by consequence, each with the section, the quoted or paraphrased evidence, and
   the required correction.
3. What could not be checked and why.
4. What the review did not do: it did not execute, benchmark, or select a runtime, and it grants no
   authority.
